name: Commodity currencies predict commodity prices

origin.source_title: Can Exchange Rates Forecast Commodity Prices? (Quarterly Journal of Economics 125(3), 2010)

how_it_works.simple: When the Australian, Canadian and New Zealand dollars rise, commodity prices tend to rise in the following months. So use those currencies as a signal to own or sell commodities.
how_it_works.analogy: Like reading the odds to guess the result: the currency market prices in news about demand before commodity prices catch up.
how_it_works.precise: Regress next-quarter changes in commodity price indices on this quarter's changes in commodity-currency exchange rates. Chen et al. find robust out-of-sample predictability over samples ending in 2008, and that the reverse direction (commodities predicting currencies) is notably less robust, consistent with exchange rates being forward looking.

rule: Monthly: average the past 3-month returns of AUD, CAD and NZD against USD; hold energy futures long when positive and short when negative, volatility-scaled.
data_needed: Daily AUD, CAD, NZD spot (FRED H.10)
economic_rationale: Exchange rates are asset prices that react to expected future commodity demand; spot commodity prices respond to current supply and demand imbalances.
why_it_might_fail: The paper's gains are statistical (lower forecast error), not trading returns; the link may have changed after 2008; energy futures are only part of the commodity indices the paper forecasts.

reported_results.source: Chen, Rogoff and Rossi (2010), NBER w13901
reported_results.market: AUD, CAD, NZD, ZAR, CLP and commodity price indices
reported_results.notes: Abstract: commodity currency exchange rates "have remarkably robust power in predicting global commodity prices, both in-sample and out-of-sample"; the reverse is "notably less robust". No trading Sharpe ratio reported.

post_publication_evidence: Ferraro, Rogoff and Rossi (2015) find the oil and Canadian dollar link is mostly same-day and absent at monthly and quarterly frequency, consistent with this entry's direction.

relevance.reason: Turns our failed oil-to-currency idea around in the direction the evidence supports; testable from 2008Q2, outside the paper's sample.

research.notes: Added from RES-0011 and RES-0012 on 2026-10-21.
